title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/14/2026
Reason for Admission: Transient ischemic attack

Vitals: BP 138/84, HR 76, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6F

Review of Systems:
Neurological: Positive for temporary numbness/weakness.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath.
Other: Negative.

HPI: Patient is an 80-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department following a sudden episode of focal neurological deficits. Symptoms were noted to be fleeting, with a transient ischemic attack resolving completely within one hour of onset. She denied any loss of consciousness or severe headache.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for observation and workup of a suspected transient ischemic attack. A non-contrast MRI of the brain was performed, which showed no evidence of a completed event. Neurological examinations remained stable throughout the stay. She was started on aspirin and advised on lifestyle modifications.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Transient ischemic attack

Discharge Medications:
- Aspirin 81mg daily

Follow-up: Follow up with neurology in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Transient ischemic attack: G45.9 (no HCC). There is no infarction, so it is not a stroke.

distractors.why: Symptoms resolved and MRI shows no infarction: TIA, not stroke.
